subject: GK
text: Who was the first President of independent India?
explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad served as the first President of India from 1950 to 1962, and remains the longest-serving President of India.

subject: GK
text: Which Indian state is famously known as the 'Spice Garden of India'?
explanation: Kerala is known as the Spice Garden of India because of its rich diversity of spices like black pepper, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves.

subject: GK
text: Which is the smallest country in the world by land area?
explanation: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, covering an area of only about 0.49 square kilometers (121 acres) and surrounded by Rome, Italy.

subject: GK
text: What is the chemical formula of common table salt?
explanation: Common table salt is chemically known as Sodium Chloride, represented by the chemical formula NaCl.

subject: GK
text: Which is the largest animal currently living on Earth?
explanation: The Blue Whale is the largest animal ever known to have lived on Earth, reaching lengths of up to 30 meters and weights of over 150 tons.

subject: GK
text: Which is the national flower of India?
explanation: The Nelumbo nucifera, commonly known as the Lotus, is the national flower of India, representing purity, beauty, and divinity.

subject: GK
text: Who served as the first Governor-General of independent India in 1947?
explanation: Lord Mountbatten served as the last Viceroy of British India and the first Governor-General of independent India until June 1948, when he was succeeded by C. Rajagopalachari.

subject: GK
text: In which year was the First Battle of Panipat fought, marking the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India?
explanation: The First Battle of Panipat was fought in 1526 between the invading forces of Babur and the Lodi Dynasty, leading to the establishment of the Mughal Empire.

subject: GK
text: Which layer of the Earth's atmosphere contains the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays?
explanation: The ozone layer is found in the lower region of the Stratosphere, which lies above the Troposphere and below the Mesosphere.

subject: GK
text: The local self-government 'Panchayati Raj System' was first officially introduced in 1959 in which Indian state?
explanation: The Panchayati Raj System was inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on 2 October 1959 in Nagaur district of Rajasthan.

subject: GK
text: Which Asian country is historically known as the 'Land of the White Elephants'?
explanation: Thailand is known as the Land of White Elephants because white elephants are considered sacred animals and symbols of royal power and good fortune in Thai culture.

subject: GK
text: What does the term 'Inflation' represent in macroeconomics?
explanation: Inflation is a general, sustained increase in the prices of goods and services in an economy over time, which reduces the purchasing power of money.

options.text: A decline in general price level
A general rise in price levels

subject: GK
text: Which committee, appointed in 1957, recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system in India?
explanation: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended the establishment of a three-tier local self-government system consisting of Gram Panchayats, Panchayat Samitis, and Zilla Parishads.

subject: GK
text: Which Mughal Emperor constructed the famous Red Fort (Lal Qila) in Delhi after shifting his capital from Agra?
explanation: Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the construction of the Red Fort in 1638 when he decided to shift his capital from Agra to Delhi (Shahjahanabad).

subject: GK
text: Which is the largest natural freshwater lake in India, located in Jammu and Kashmir?
explanation: Wular Lake is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia, fed by the Jhelum River, and plays a major role in the regional ecology.

subject: GK
text: Who was the first Indian woman to successfully scale Mount Everest, achieving the feat in 1984?
explanation: Bachendri Pal scaled Mount Everest on 23 May 1984, becoming the first Indian woman and the fifth woman in the world to reach the summit.

subject: GK
text: What is the official currency of Japan?
explanation: The Japanese Yen, symbolized as ¥, is the official currency of Japan and is the third most traded currency in the foreign exchange market.

subject: GK
text: Which country hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?
explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896 under the auspices of the newly created International Olympic Committee (IOC).

subject: GK
text: The landmark 'Tashkent Agreement' of 1966 was signed between India and Pakistan following which armed conflict?
explanation: The Tashkent Agreement was signed on 10 January 1966 by Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and President Ayub Khan to resolve the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965.

subject: GK
text: Who was the author of the ancient Sanskrit political play 'Mudrarakshasa', which narrates the ascent of Chandragupta Maurya to power?
explanation: Vishakhadatta was a Sanskrit poet and playwright who wrote the historical drama 'Mudrarakshasa' during the late Gupta period.

subject: GK
text: The 'Karakum Desert', known for its famous 'Door to Hell' gas crater, is located in which Central Asian nation?
explanation: The Karakum Desert occupies about 70 percent of the area of Turkmenistan and contains the Darvaza gas crater, a natural gas field that has been burning since 1971.

subject: GK
text: Which economic model served as the blueprint and foundation for India's Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), emphasizing heavy industrialization?
explanation: The Mahalanobis Model, formulated by Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis, prioritized rapid development of basic and heavy industries to promote self-reliance.

subject: GK
text: The 'Nokrek Biosphere Reserve', which is one of the key habitats of the red panda and a major UNESCO World Network site, is located in which Indian state?
explanation: The Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is located in the West Garo Hills district of Meghalaya, and comprises the Nokrek National Park.

subject: GK
text: Which visionary Indian physicist is celebrated as the 'Father of the Indian Space Program' and was instrumental in establishing ISRO?
explanation: Dr. Vikram Sarabhai was a pioneer who established the Physical Research Laboratory and successfully convinced the government of the importance of space research, founding INCOSPAR (later ISRO).

subject: GK
text: The international boundary line between India and China in the eastern sector, proposed during the Simla Accord of 1914, is known as which line?
explanation: The McMahon Line is the boundary line proposed by Sir Henry McMahon at the Simla Convention, which is recognized by India as its official border but contested by China.
